text: If the doctor has been killed. <break time="0.8s" /> Why would the murderer stay in his room. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked Utterson. <break time="0.8s" /> Who thought the story too wild to believe. <break time="0.8s" /> Poole explained that for a whole week. <break time="0.8s" /> The thing in the cabinet. <break time="0.8s" /> Had been crying out night and day. <break time="0.8s" /> For some kind of medicine. <break time="0.8s" /> It threw written orders onto the stairs. <break time="0.8s" /> And Poole had been sent. <break time="0.8s" /> To every chemist in London. <break time="0.8s" /> Only to have the drug returned as impure. <break time="0.8s" /> He showed one of the notes. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was in the doctors handwriting. <break time="0.8s" /> And ended. <break time="0.8s" /> For Gods sake find me some of the old. <break time="0.8s" /> This is certainly the doctors hand. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Utterson. <break time="0.8s" /> But Poole cried. <break time="0.8s" /> What does the handwriting matter, sir. <break time="0.8s" /> I have seen him. <break time="0.8s" /> He had come into the laboratory one day. <break time="0.8s" /> And found the creature digging among the boxes. <break time="0.8s" /> With a mask over its face. <break time="0.8s" /> The moment it saw him. <break time="0.8s" /> It gave a cry like a rat. <break time="0.8s" /> And ran upstairs. <break time="0.8s" /> And Pooles hair stood on end with fear. <break time="0.8s" /> Utterson suggested that the doctor had a terrible illness. <break time="0.8s" /> One that changed his looks and voice. <break time="0.8s" /> And made him hide behind a mask. <break time="0.8s" /> But Poole disagreed. <break time="0.8s" /> For his master was tall and well built. <break time="0.8s" /> While the thing he had seen. <break time="0.8s" /> Was more like a dwarf.
